import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Combine 'date' and 'time' columns and convert to datetime objects
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract the hour of the day and the day of the week
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour
df['day_of_week'] = df['datetime'].dt.day_name()

# --- Data Aggregation ---
# Create a pivot table to aggregate total sales by day and hour
sales_by_day_hour = df.pivot_table(
    values='total',
    index='day_of_week',
    columns='hour',
    aggfunc='sum'
).fillna(0)

# Ensure the days of the week are in chronological order
day_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
sales_by_day_hour = sales_by_day_hour.reindex(day_order)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the style and figure size
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(18, 9))

# Create the heatmap
ax = sns.heatmap(
    sales_by_day_hour,
    cmap='viridis',
    linewidths=.5,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".0f",  # Format annotations as integers
    annot_kws={"size": 8},
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'}
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set the title and axis labels with appropriate font sizes
plt.title('Peak Sales Times: Hourly Sales by Day of the Week', fontsize=20, weight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=14)

# Improve readability of tick labels
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(rotation=0, fontsize=10)

# Format the color bar labels
cbar = ax.collections[0].colorbar
cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.StrMethodFormatter('${x:,.0f}'))

# --- Save the Figure ---
# Save the final plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

    values='total',
    index='day_of_week',

    fmt=".0f",  # Format annotations as integers

    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'}
